newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht eases offshore, interbank falls late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht eases offshore, interbank falls late.

text.p: Thai baht eased in the offshore market late on Monday but barely changed in the domestic market where it moved in a narrow range, dealers said.
The baht was quoted around 24.150/24.250 to the dollar late offshore against 23.90/24.00 early on Monday. In the onshore market, it was quoted at 25.740/25.750 compared with 25.740/25.760 earlier.
The Bank of Thailand set the midrate on Monday at 25.75 baht per dollar
Dealers said pressure to sell dollar to buy the baht in the offshore market had eased as some foreign investors unwound stocks last week to acquire much-needed baht.
"But the demand is still there. Those with stock holdings were convinced it would be cheaper to dump shares than to borrow baht or sell dollars," said one offshore dealers.
Thailand's two-tier market, imposed last month to cut baht supplies to speculators, remained in place and was expected by the market to last another few months.
The overnight interbank rate edged down to 11.00-12.00 late on Monday versus 13.50-14.00 percent earlier in the day.
Dealers said liquidity was ample due to central bank fund injections, dollar selling and foreign inflows.
"The central bank's bond repurchase rate was down from the morning, indicating it wanted to keep the overnight rate down," said a dealer at one major foreign bank.
"There were also foreign inflows which entered through short-dated swaps," she said.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium was quoted around 15/20 satangs to the dollar against 17/22 earlier in the local market and 110/140 satangs in the offshore market.
